:::{#exm-entropy-chain-rule-n-copies}
#### Chain rule for entropy along a chain of noisy copies
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X_1$ be a fair coin toss, coded $0$ or $1$.
Let $X_2$ be a noisy copy of $X_1$ that flips it with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.2$,
and let $X_3$ be a noisy copy of $X_2$ that flips it with probability $0.2$,
independently of $X_1$ given $X_2$.
The chunk builds the [joint probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf) of $(X_1, X_2, X_3)$
and compares their [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy), in [bits](#def-bit),
with the sum in @thm-entropy-chain-rule-n.

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
flip <- 0.2
channel <- matrix(
  data = c(1 - flip, flip, flip, 1 - flip),
  nrow = 2,
  byrow = TRUE
)
joint <- array(data = 0, dim = c(2, 2, 2))
for (x1 in 1:2) {
  for (x2 in 1:2) {
    for (x3 in 1:2) {
      joint[x1, x2, x3] <- 0.5 * channel[x1, x2] * channel[x2, x3]
    }
  }
}
h_joint <- -sum(joint * log2(joint))
h_coin <- -flip * log2(flip) - (1 - flip) * log2(1 - flip)
h_sum <- 1 + h_coin + h_coin
c(h_joint = h_joint, h_sum = h_sum)
```

The first term of the sum is $\entropyf{X_1} = 1$ [bit](#def-bit).
Given $X_1$, the variable $X_2$ is a coin with flip probability $0.2$,
and given $(X_1, X_2)$ the variable $X_3$ is the same kind of coin,
so each of the other two terms is $`r round(h_coin, 3)`$ bits.
The sum is $`r round(h_sum, 3)`$ bits,
which equals $\entropyf{X_1, X_2, X_3} = `r round(h_joint, 3)`$ bits.

:::
